gotcha #7 (tu93): env.reset() is NOT idempotent -- it leaves a parity-toggling hidden state (same path, 6 reset+replays -> levels [1,2,1,2,1,2]). A reuse-one-env replay/deepcopy search detects parity-CONTINGENT wins that fail the fresh-env reproduction gate (gate correctly rejects -- no false claim). Fix: OfflineSolver branch_mode='fresh_env' (a brand-new env per candidate eval) so each evaluation sees the same pristine parity-0 the gate uses. Detect by replaying ONE path on N fresh envs vs 1 env reset N times: if levels differ, reset is non-idempotent.

recommended.action_model: Keyboard ACTION1-4 move the selected splitter after display-rotation remapping; ACTION6 selects splitter sprites from offline-derived display centers; ACTION5 commits the spill. L2 tail selects the two len3 splitters and moves them to the derived target placements. L3+: ACTION1-4 move the currently-selected piece (no rotation observed); commits are cheap to retry (the spill animates, drains, and pieces keep their positions on failure) but appear resource-limited via a per-commit border-pixel counter that resets each level.
reusable_gotchas: L2 has dojfslwbg=180, so external keyboard directions and click coordinates are display-rotated before the game maps them back to grid space.
The win predicate is not just visible piece placement; ACTION5 starts a spill, and success requires every repwkzbkhxl block to be marked while no waoewejnqzc wall is touched.
Failed commit states can spend search time in spill animation; use a bounded spill predicate to evaluate candidate placements before replay-gating.
Use fresh-env branching for this adapter; replaying L1 on a reused advanced sp80 env does not reconstruct the L2 start state that the reproduction gate sees from a pristine offline arcade.

L3-L4 SPILL-ROUTING PHYSICS mechanic (2026-07-11, claude-fable-5, independently re-verified by the outer loop): flow direction alternates per level (L3 towers shoot vines UPWARD; L4 flips to a ceiling spout pouring DOWNWARD; L5 reverts to upward). SPLITTER BARS: a stream hitting a bar runs along its far side to both ends and re-emits 3px branch streams just past each end (streams merge when feeding the same bar). The blue border/ceiling band AND the grey floor are BOTH lethal on contact -- every stream must terminate inside a target; branches pushed off the board EDGE (not into a wall) vanish harmlessly and are the only safe disposal in L3. THE SUBTLE KILLER, vertical clearance: a bar's run occupies the 3 pixel-rows on its far side, so parking a bar exactly one cell beyond another bar's face BLOCKS that bar's run from spreading, silently deleting its branch outputs (cost a failed commit in L4). EMBEDDED SOURCES (new at L4): a long bar can carry its own 3px source segment that drips a stream wherever the bar is moved -- a second, movable spout. Pieces move on per-piece 3px sub-lattices with per-piece positional caps (e.g. L3 bars cannot rise above grid-row 4); measure piece and target positions from the frame programmatically, off-by-one eyeballing wastes commits.

L5 SOLVED (2026-07-11, gpt-5.6-sol via codex, post-wa30 breadth campaign round 2): the color-15 L-piece is a fluid elbow/diverter, NOT a key inserted into the wall sculpture -- at its x=14 minimum, a splitter branch entering its lower-right leg is redirected horizontally into the wall notch. Winning positions: color-15 elbow at x=14,y=35; 12px bar at x=20..31,y=47; 15px bar at x=23..37,y=29; 9px bar at x=41..49,y=47; commit with ACTION5. The frame after the L4 win still visually shows the prior layout even though levels_completed is already 4 -- the NEXT action initializes L5's stable rendering. Independently re-verified by the outer loop: 5x fresh env.reset() + replay via the fixed resolver, all 5 confirmed reached_level=5, state=GameState.NOT_FINISHED. L6 was explored (two oriented color-15 elbows, a vertical color-8 splitter, an embedded-source horizontal splitter, two left sockets, one right socket, a bottom arch) but not won this session -- several geometry-consistent placements tried, none completed the level.

L6 progress round 3, still HONEST NULL (2026-07-12, gpt-5.6-sol via codex): tested four rendered-geometry routing families (centered and horizontally-shifted embedded-source splitters, both assignments of the oppositely-oriented elbows to the side branches, a target-aligned vertical splitter at x=14,y=26) -- none won. Genuinely new finding: L6 has a FINITE WHOLE-LEVEL action budget, not merely a per-commit counter -- after 79 exploratory suffix actions, an ordinary movement action ended the episode with an empty terminal frame (this had not been observed in the prior L6 exploration). The selected piece renders as color 9 (unselected splitters are color 8, unselected elbows color 15), confirmed reliable for rendered-frame-only position tracking. No new level banked; the whole-level budget finding narrows future attempts (route planning must now also respect a hard action ceiling, not just the per-commit border-pixel counter documented earlier).

L6 progress round 4, still HONEST NULL (2026-07-12, gpt-5.6-sol via codex, round-4 breadth campaign, results/outer_loop_fable5_sp80_probe.json): frontier stays at level 5 -- this is the FINAL level (win_levels=6). New geometric finding: elbow routing depends on one-cell alignment -- a downward stream aimed at an elbow's vertical stem can spill down its inner side AS WELL AS turn (a double-leak), while offsetting the elbow so the stream meets its HORIZONTAL arm instead eliminates one leakage path and fills previously-unreachable side sockets. Offsetting one elbow by one cell filled all four visible sockets but the animation still showed an extra downward spill missing the bottom cup; a symmetric offset of the other elbow was attempted but ended the live episode (GAME_OVER) before any level-up, confirming round 3's finding that ACTION5 commits are a scarce resource independent of the whole-level action limit (5 commits exhausted the episode here). A compressed 36-action one-commit candidate for the hypothesized corrected layout was fresh-reset reproduce()-gated and reached only level 5 -- filling all four visible sockets is confirmed INSUFFICIENT while any stray stream remains; at least one final routing or hidden condition is still unresolved. No new level banked.

L6 SOLVED, FULL GAME CLEAR round 5 (2026-07-12, claude-fable-5, first fable-5 leg of the campaign, results/outer_loop_fable5_sp80_probe.json): resolves round 4's "at least one final routing or hidden condition is still unresolved" with a precise geometric diagnosis, not a new mechanic. Round 4's layout already colored all four sockets, but the right branch struck the SOLID TOP of the right socket at y=29..31 even though the socket glyph visibly changed color (a glyph-color change does not mean the stream actually entered through the open side). Moving only the right-turn elbow down exactly ONE 3-pixel cell (y=29..34 -> y=32..37) shifts the outflow to y=32..34, through the socket's actual open side, and wins live. Compressed to a 37-action suffix after the 278-action prefix (315 total); fresh-reset reproduce() passed with reached_level=6. Independently re-verified by the outer loop: 5x fresh env.reset() + replay via a new resolver priority branch, all 5 confirmed level=6, state=GameState.WIN -- the game's full 6 levels are now cleared.

FULL CLEAR, L6 (2026-07-11, gpt-5.6-sol via codex, post-wa30 breadth campaign round 2): L6 is a five-sprite marker-pair puzzle. The G-hook and n-glyph rotate through four ACTION5 orientations; the tall bar is a rigid two-marker connector; the three-marker arm stretches one marker 3px per press through 4 stops, ping-ponging; the winding snake grows non-uniformly from 2 to 6 markers via ACTION5, and DESELECTING/ RESELECTING it appears to reset or reverse its ping-pong direction (do not predict remaining presses from the direction observed before deselecting). Solved via an exact-cover constraint search over marker constellations, then executed the placement live. The source agent honestly flagged the win as reproduction_verified=false (only 5 of 700 steps remained after the live win, not enough for a fresh gate) -- the outer loop independently ran the canonical reproduction gate AND 4 additional fresh env.reset()+replay trials before recording anything: all 5 returned reached_level=6 AND state=GameState.WIN. cn04 is a confirmed full clear.

L4-L5 SHAPE-VARIANT ESCALATION mechanic (2026-07-11, claude-fable-5, independently re-verified by the outer loop): the core loop is consistent across L4-L6 -- ACTION6-click selects a sprite (revealing its 8-colored 3x3 markers; unselected sprites hide markers), ACTION1-4 translate the selection in 3px steps, and the level completes the INSTANT every marker on every sprite coincides with exactly one marker from another sprite (paired markers render green, live feedback -- survey by clicking each sprite before planning). L4: ACTION5 rigidly rotates 90 degrees; solved as vector algebra (a closed 4-cycle of marker-offset vectors). L5 BREAKS the rotation assumption: ACTION5 instead cycles each sprite through a FORM CATALOG (e.g. a snake ping-pongs through lengths 3-7 with a black growth-head marker that vanishes at max length; other sprites include zero-marker EMPTY forms in their cycle). Solve by exhaustively cataloging every sprite's form catalog empirically (a handful of ACTION5 presses per sprite), then constraint-solving for the unique feasible configuration covering every marker 1:1 -- rigid pairing under a single fixed form is provably infeasible once variant cycling is active. One documented anomaly: a transient ALL-GREEN state did not fire the win once (suspected subtle mis-pairing after an accidental displacement); tearing one sprite away and rebuilding the identical configuration fired the win immediately -- if everything looks paired but nothing fires, try a rebuild before assuming the model is wrong.
